rules.rule: No invented reviews or testimonials are shown as real. Placeholder reviews are clearly labelled, and all are replaced with genuine ones before launch.
rules.why: Fake reviews are a banned practice under the DMCC Act 2024 (Schedule 20 para 13), in force since 6 April 2025, and advertisers must hold evidence that each testimonial is genuine (CAP 3.47).
rules.check: List every review and testimonial on the site. Each traces to a real source (platform, date, first name) held on file, and nothing labelled as a sample remains at launch.

evidence.reason: Primary legislation and the regulator's code, read in the original. The reason to follow it is legal, not a conversion effect.

rules.rule: Don't say that dates, stock or a price are limited, or show a countdown, unless it is true and driven by live data or a real, fixed deadline.
rules.why: Falsely saying a product is available only for a limited time is a banned practice (DMCC Act 2024 Schedule 20 para 7; CAP 3.30). The CMA fined Wayfair £4.8m in October 2026 for deals that carried on past their deadlines.

evidence.reason: Banned outright when false: legislation, the CAP Code and a CMA penalty, read in the original. Genuine scarcity is allowed.

rules.rule: Advertising tags and cookies run only after the visitor consents. Analytics may run without consent only where the PECR statistical-purposes exception fully applies: clear information and a simple, free way to object.
rules.why: PECR reg 6 and Schedule A1 (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, in force 5 February 2026) require consent unless an exception applies. The statistical exception doesn't cover advertising (ICO).
rules.check: In a fresh private window, open a landing page and ignore the banner: the browser's developer tools show no advertising cookies and no ad pixels firing. Reject and check again. If analytics runs before consent, the privacy notice explains it and offers a one-click objection.

evidence.reason: Primary legislation and ICO guidance, read in the original.

rules.why: UK GDPR Article 13 requires the information at the time the data is collected. It changed in 2026: notices must now mention the right to complain to the controller (Art 13(2)(ca), from 19 June 2026).

evidence.reason: Primary legislation, read in the original.

rules.rule: If a quiz asks about health, sex life or sexual orientation, or is designed to infer them, treat the answers as special category data: ask the minimum, avoid free text, and get separate explicit consent first.
rules.why: UK GDPR Article 9 prohibits processing this data without a condition such as explicit consent. The ICO counts inferences too, where you intend to make them or act on them.

evidence.reason: Article 9 and ICO guidance, read in the original. Whether a given quiz triggers them depends on its questions. The RGC summary also recommends a data protection impact assessment; that step wasn't checked.
